# Midpoint stochastic domination and failure of the capacity-mean OC budget

This note proves a general directional domination lemma and applies it
to the exact five-dimensional simplex-fiber example in
`candidate e13ef2bc2dcc3baf`. The result is
an obstruction to a proposed intermediate rule, not to OC itself.

## 1. An endpoint capacity is an actual one-dimensional measure

Let A and C be positive-volume convex bodies in R^d, with volumes
0<a<=c. Fix a nonzero continuous functional u and define

 A_u(t)=|A intersect {u.x>=t}|,
 C_u(t)=|C intersect {u.x>=t}|,
 K_u(t)=inf_(v in R)[A_u(t+v)+C_u(t-v)].           (1)

Then K_u is the closed survival function of a finite nonnegative
one-dimensional measure kappa_u of mass a and compact support.

Indeed K_u is nonincreasing and takes values in [0,a]; the upper bound
is attained as a comparison by taking one endpoint cap full and the
other empty. If l_A,l_C and h_A,h_C are the minimum and maximum values
of u on the two bodies, then

 K_u(t)=a for t<=(l_A+l_C)/2,
 K_u(t)=0 for t>=(h_A+h_C)/2.                    (2)

For the first assertion, if both endpoint caps were not full, their
thresholds would have sum strictly greater than l_A+l_C. Thus at least
one is full, and its mass is at least a. For the second choose the tilt
which puts both thresholds at or above the two respective maxima.
The boundary of each nonzero-functional cap has d-volume zero.

The fiber cap functions are globally Lipschitz, with constants bounded
by their maximal (d-1)-section volume divided by |u|. Consequently the
functions inside the infimum in (1) have a common Lipschitz constant
in t, so their infimum K_u is Lipschitz as well. It is therefore
continuous. The monotone continuous function with the two limiting
values in (2) determines the asserted measure without atoms. No
log-concavity or power concavity of that measure is required.

## 2. Every midpoint coupling is stochastically dominated

Let sigma be any measure satisfying 0<=sigma<=1_C dx and sigma(C)=a.
Let pi be any coupling whose two marginals are 1_A dx and sigma, and
let eta be its pushforward under (x,y)->(x+y)/2. This is a measure of
mass a, with centroid

 g_eta=(g_A+g_sigma)/2.                         (3)

Then for every real t,

 eta{u.x>=t} <= K_u(t).                         (4)

For each paired source point, if u.(x+y)/2>=t, it is impossible that
both u.x<t+v and u.y<t-v. Hence the exact pointwise closed-halfspace
indicator inequality gives

 eta{u.x>=t}
 <= A_u(t+v)+sigma{u.x>=t-v}
 <= A_u(t+v)+C_u(t-v)

for every v. Taking the infimum proves (4), including boundary mass
of the midpoint measure.

Both measures in (4) have mass a and bounded support. Integrate their
survival functions over a common bounded interval containing those
supports; the elementary identity

 integral X dnu = L nu(R)+integral_L^U nu([t,infinity))dt

then proves

 integral t dkappa_u(t) >= a u.g_eta.           (5)

In particular (5) does not require eta to have a density or a uniform
convex support. It follows directly from all-threshold domination.

## 3. Transfer from a failed candidate point to a failed capacity mean

Add a middle convex body B of volume b>0, and assume (A+C)/2 subset B.
Let the actual three-layer mixed measure have fibers A,B,C. Its
optimized directional survival function is

 V_u(t)=|B intersect {u.x>=t}|+K_u(t).           (6)

It is the survival of a measure of mass D=b+a, as distinct from the
original mixed mass M=a+b+c. Let h(u) be the mean of this measure.
For any sigma and midpoint coupling as above define the actual point

 y=(b g_B+a g_eta)/(b+a).                       (7)

Since g_eta belongs to (A+C)/2, the point y belongs to B. Equation (5)
implies the directional comparison

 h(u)>=u.y.                                   (8)

Suppose an actual ambient cap

 H={u.x+v z>=t_0}

contains (0,y) and has mixed mass strictly below some target T. Since
t_0<=u.y, the cap with the same normal through (0,y) is contained in H.
Equations (6),(8) and monotonicity therefore give

 V_u(h(u)) <= V_u(u.y) <= mu(H) < T.            (9)

Thus a failed candidate of the precise form (7) yields a direction in
which taking the optimized capacity law's own mean also fails the same
absolute target. This implication concerns a direction that may depend
on the failed point. It constructs no common point with all-direction
depth.

## 4. Exact failure of the OC target for a derived capacity mean

Use the body from `candidate e13ef2bc2dcc3baf`.
All measures in this section use the same reference dx/|B|, where B
is its standard 5-simplex. Thus b=c=1, 0<a<10^(-5), and M=2+a.
The homogeneous inequalities of sections 1--3 are unchanged by this
common measure rescaling. That file proves all of the following
data by exact rational inequalities:

 A=(2-q)D,  C=qD,  (A+C)/2=D subset B,
 r=497/3000,
 max_D x_1=r,
 (g_D)_1=5r/6,
 H_1={x_1+(1-q)r z>=1/6-(2/25)a},
 mu(H_1)<gamma_5(1+a/2).                       (10)

The last bound is in these same relative volume units. The cap H_1
excludes both endpoint fibers, by the exact support computations in
that file.

Take sigma=a times uniform probability on C. It is dominated by the
chosen reference volume on C because c=1 and a<1. Pair homothetically corresponding
points of A and C; their midpoint distribution is a times normalized
volume on D. Thus g_eta=g_D, and (7) becomes

 y_mix=(g_B+a g_D)/(1+a).                      (11)

This point belongs to H_1 directly, without choosing between the two
covering caps of the original example. Indeed

 1/6-(g_D)_1=(1-5r)/6=103/3600<2/25,

and therefore

 (y_mix)_1=1/6-[a/(1+a)](103/3600)
            >1/6-(2/25)a.

Apply (9) with u=e_1 and T=gamma_5 M/2. It yields the exact strict
inequality

 V_(e_1)(h(e_1))<gamma_5 M/2.                  (12)

The derived capacity law has total D=1+a, so in normalized terms

 V_(e_1)(h(e_1))/D < gamma_5 M/(2D)
   =gamma_5 [1-(D-M/2)/D],
 D-M/2=a/2>0.                                 (13)

Consequently the natural proposed deficit bound with the normalized
capacity slack, namely gamma_d[1-(D-M/2)/D], is false for the law's own
directional mean. The failure occurs with all three fibers simplices,
all positive and strictly nonheavy. No value of h(e_1) needs to be
approximated: (5),(8),(10) prove (12) exactly.

This does not contradict OC. The original selector example leaves other
middle-fiber points available, and an actual all-halfspace OC escape
point for that particular body has been proved separately. The failed
assertion is solely a universal capacity-mean rule.
